newsitem.title: THAILAND: Motorola wins $120 mln expansion project.
newsitem.headline: Motorola wins $120 mln expansion project.

text.p: Total Access Communication Plc said on Wednesday it awarded a $120 million expansion project to Motorola's Asia Pacific Cellular Infrastructure Group to expand and upgrade its cellular phone service in Thailand.
The company said in a statement the expansion will increase TAC's overall network capacity and extend geographic coverage in Bangkok and Thai provinces.
Motorola will upgrade many existing analog cell sites to a digital-ready Narrow-band Advanced Mobile Phone Service (N-AMPS) platform with Linear Power Amplifiers (LPAs).

N-AMPS provide three times the number of cellular voice channels as AMPS. The LPAs designed and deployed by Motorola provide remote tuning and space-efficient use of more voice channels, the statement said.
The announcement was made during a ceremony where TAC signed an agreement with the U.S. Export-Import Bank for a $104.8 million loan to support the sale of an advanced phone system.
The loan was to assist in the sale of the phone service by Motorola. The loan was the EXIM bank's largest authorisation in Thailand for fiscal year 1996, the statement said.
